claims.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL to Pulumi, and orchestrate Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly in Pulumi.

The Pulumi Terraform provider exposes a `terraform.state.S3Reference` resource taking `bucket` and `key` arguments and a `getOutput` method, for referencing Terraform state stored in S3 (also referenced as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` in the Automation API example).

The same `S3Reference` is accessed as `terraform.state.S3Reference` in one example (with no import) and as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` from `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` import in another; the `@pulumi/pulumi` package exposes a `terraform` namespace.
`new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` with `getOutput("vpcId")` is valid StackReference usage.
The `aws.ecs.Cluster` resource accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` set to "DEFAULT".
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.

`pulumi import` takes the form `pulumi import <type> <name> <id>`, e.g., `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`, and types `aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet` and `aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster` are valid; the ECS cluster import ID is the cluster name.
State ownership can be transferred gradually, resource-by-resource, from Terraform to Pulumi.
The `getOutput` method on a Terraform state reference returns a Promise that can be awaited and filtered as an array of resources with `type` and `name`.
The `@pulumi/policy` package exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`, with policies using `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"` and `validateResource`.
Pulumi policies (Policy as Code) can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.
The `aws.s3.Bucket` resource has an `acl` property that can be `public-read` or `public-read-write`.

The Automation API in `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` provides `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` with `stackName`, `projectName`, `program`, plus `stack.setConfig` and `stack.up({onOutput})` returning `outputs`.
The Automation API lets you embed Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.

Component resources can wrap Terraform-backed infrastructure so that developers create resources without knowing they depend on Terraform-managed resources, leaving multi-tool complexity to the platform team.
`pulumi.ComponentResource` with `super(type, name, {}, opts)` and `registerOutputs` is the way to define component resources.
An ECS Fargate task definition with cpu "256" and memory "512" is a valid Fargate configuration.
